cohort: The study included 902 pregnant women, of whom 224 were adolescents, compared against older pregnant women.
finding: Adolescent pregnant women demonstrated significantly higher rates of Group B Streptococcus infection, nicotine use, and greater mean blood loss during delivery, while their newborns exhibited lower mean birth weight and length, and higher incidences of neonatal complications and NICU admissions compared to older pregnant women.
mod_finding: Adolescent patients experienced higher mean blood loss during both vaginal births (500 mL) and cesarean sections (1050 mL).
birth_weight: Mean birth weight for newborns from adolescent pregnancies was 3199 g.
